learning_objective: Subtract the input zero point, multiply int8 operands, accumulate in int32 and convert the accumulated result back to real/output units.
core_conclusion: Quantized MAC operates on centered integer codes; the int32 sum represents a real value scaled by the product of input and weight scales.

terminology.scope: Official terminology basis from saved course research; all numerical examples are explicitly illustrative.

scenes.heading: Integer codes include an offset
lines: Input zero point = 3; weight zero point = 0.
scenes.change: Each input subtracts3, changing5,7,4 into2,4,1; the weight row stays2,−1,3.
scenes.cause: A zero point encodes real zero, so multiplication uses centered codes.
scenes.result: The visible operands entering multiplication are centered values.
scenes.timing_reason: 3.5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 2.5 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Multiply corresponding entries
lines: Match each input with its weight.
scenes.change: Each pair descends into a multiplication cell and creates a signed product; the negative weight creates−4.
scenes.cause: Dot products multiply matching entries before addition.
scenes.result: Positive and negative product bars are visible.
scenes.timing_reason: 3.5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 2.5 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Accumulate in int32
lines: The partial sum changes after each addition.
scenes.change: Products enter sequentially; accumulator changes0→4→0→3, with the negative term visibly cancelling the first.
scenes.cause: The wide accumulator sums integer products without narrowing after each term.
scenes.result: The final accumulator is3, not the largest individual product.
scenes.timing_reason: 6 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Restore the real units
scenes.change: The sum3 passes through the scale product0.02 and becomes0.06; a paired real-valued dot product resolves to the same value.
scenes.cause: Input and weight scales multiply through the dot product.
scenes.result: Both computation paths agree for this illustrative no-bias example.
scenes.timing_reason: 3.5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 2.5 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Encode the output if needed
scenes.change: Output0.06 divides by0.01 and adds−2 to produce code4; inverse reconstruction yields0.06.
scenes.cause: A next integer operator may require its own activation scale and zero point.
scenes.result: The output code is not the accumulator value:4 versus3.
scenes.timing_reason: 3.5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 2.5 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

final_title: Quantized Multiply and Accumulate: Integer Products to Codes
title: Quantized Multiply and Accumulate: Integer Products to Codes
prompt:
Create a 33-second silent English animation of Quantized Multiply and Accumulate. At 0–6 s, subtract input zero point 3 from codes [5, 7, 4] to obtain [2, 4, 1]. At 6–12 s, multiply by weights [2, −1, 3] to form products [4, −4, 3]. At 12–21 s, move each product into an int32 accumulator whose sum changes 0 to 4 to 0 to 3. At 21–27 s, multiply by scales 0.2 × 0.1 to obtain real output 0.06. At 27–33 s, requantize with output scale 0.01 and zero point −2 to produce int8 code 4; omit bias in this example.

Render a 1920×1080, 16:9 MP4 at 30 fps with no audio, using Helvetica Neue and line height 1.45. Use background layers #0e0e0e, #171b1c and #212629; input #56b4e9, operations #e69f00, results #009e73, clipping or rejection #d55e00, and secondary weights #cc79a7, with strong text #f8fafc and muted text #a8b4c4. Keep concise copy left and a large numerical SVG diagram right; fade and slide labels over 12–18 frames with 10-frame staggering, and bind moving marks, values and arithmetic to the same mechanism state.
